ambiguities.description: The manager-manages-department relationship is described as 'at most one' with no mandatory statement about whether every department must have a manager. Should there be a mandatory or optional constraint on the Department side, and can a department have zero managers?

source_references.excerpt: A manager manages at most one department. Some managers are between assignments and manage none.

ambiguities.description: It is not stated whether multiple managers could manage the same department simultaneously, or whether department-to-manager is strictly one-to-one/one-to-many. Clarify the uniqueness on the Department role in the 'Manager manages Department' fact type.

source_references.excerpt: A manager manages at most one department.

ambiguities.description: PersonId is used as identifier for Person, and Employee/Manager inherit it. It is not explicitly stated whether Employee or Manager have any additional independent identifiers (e.g., employee number), which could be an overlooked identification scheme.

source_references.excerpt: Employees are persons; every employee is also a person, identified the same way.

ambiguities.description: Temporal aspect: employee-department assignment and manager-department assignment are described only as current state ('works in exactly one department', 'manages at most one department'). It is unclear if historical tracking of department assignments over time is needed.

source_references.excerpt: Every employee works in exactly one department.
A manager manages at most one department.

ambiguities.description: Granularity: DepartmentCode and DepartmentName are both unique identifiers-like attributes for Department.
